cook.title: Kitchen worker
cook.line: Bring the bowl back. We can replace the food more easily than the ceramic.

courier.title: Neighborhood courier
courier.line: I know which doors open late. The route planner only knows which ones pay.

technician.title: Maintenance worker
technician.line: Keep the old part until the new one works. That's the whole apprenticeship.

patient.title: Clinic visitor
patient.line: I traded a shift to get here. The attendant says I can stay until someone sees me.

medic.title: Clinic attendant
medic.line: You can come in without a balance. We ask your name before your account.

archivist.title: Records clerk
archivist.line: A blank entry can mean someone refused. Don't fill it in for them.

neighbor.title: Local resident
neighbor.rest: Waiting for someone to come home
neighbor.line: I used to recognize this block by the signs. Now I recognize the people waiting under them.

customer.title: Shift worker
customer.line: Five minutes with something hot. Then I can think about tomorrow.

gardener.title: Courtyard caretaker
gardener.line: That tray is seedlings. This one is what we couldn't keep alive. We count both.

commuter.title: Transit regular
commuter.line: If the lift is running, I get home before my daughter wakes. That's my timetable.

neighborhoods.name: Lantern Market
neighborhoods.premise: The free kitchen feeds the Commons, but its donated water is being billed to the same families twice. Nella keeps serving while the bowls, debts, and queues pile up.

events.name: The long lunch
events.detail: The kitchen crew serves the shift queue.

events.name: Water delivery
events.detail: Carriers unload the Commons' water allotment.

events.name: The bowl exchange
events.detail: Neighbors wash and return the kitchen's ceramics.

stages.status: A queue that never gets shorter
stages.line: They call it donated water. Nella has the receipts from the families who paid for it.

stages.contactLine: Fourteen missing diners. I know every one of them. Now we need to find out why donating water made their bills grow.
stages.line: You counted the empty places. Nella kept those portions warm anyway.

stages.contactLine: The receipts match. I'll keep them beside the counter until the kitchen has a rota that everyone can read.
stages.line: The meter counted every jug twice. Now the whole queue has seen the reading.

stages.contactLine: Take a bowl. I'm off the counter for an hour; Mina has the next shift. We still ration the water, but we don't bill the donors twice.
stages.status: The kitchen belongs to its queue
stages.line: We take turns at the counter now. The water is still rationed, but nobody charges us for donating it.

neighborhoods.name: Glass Steps
neighborhoods.premise: A cooling failure makes the clinics choose which memories stay readable. Elin suspects the priority list ranks a person's remaining payments above their wishes.

events.name: Open witness hour
events.detail: Clerks compare copies with the people who remember them.

events.name: Coolant rotation
events.detail: The maintenance crew changes the archive's cooling cells.

events.name: Consent collection
events.detail: Couriers collect sealed permissions from the clinics.

stages.status: A person's last week is warming
stages.line: The premium vault is cold. My mother's shelf isn't. They say the order is automatic.

stages.contactLine: That ordinary morning matters to its witness. I won't let the index choose for her. Check the cooling order next.
stages.line: She asked to keep one ordinary morning. The index marked it disposable.

stages.contactLine: The queue sorts by money before it reads consent. We can free duplicate space, but only if its witnesses agree.
stages.line: Elin found the payment column. We weren't imagining which shelves warmed first.

stages.contactLine: The cold space rotates now. People signed away copies, not their right to refuse. I keep both kinds of answer here.
stages.line: We rotate the cold space by consent now. I gave up a copy so someone else could keep their only one.

neighborhoods.name: Copper Walk
neighborhoods.premise: An unfinished heat line warms an empty concession office while occupied flats freeze. Merek's repair crew can redirect it, if they can protect the next shift from inheriting the debt.

events.name: Tools on the table
events.detail: Repair crews rebuild the block's worn heat couplings.

events.name: Protected break
events.detail: The outgoing crew eats while the relief crew checks in.

events.name: Shared parts run
events.detail: Couriers bring reclaimed parts to the public workbench.

stages.line: Put your hand on the office wall. Warm. Nobody's worked there in eleven years.

stages.contactLine: Twenty-three occupied flats. They were never empty; they were outside the account. Let's see where their heat went.
stages.line: Merek wrote down every flat. Including the ones the housing register calls empty.

stages.contactLine: We can reach the bypass. We also need a rota that doesn't leave the youngest worker holding eleven years of repair debt.
stages.line: The bypass is ready. We won't put an apprentice's name on the repair bond.

stages.contactLine: The office is cold and the risers take turns. My crew's eating. For once, I can tell you who's coming to relieve them.
stages.line: My room is warm for six hours. The next six belong to the upstairs family. I'll take a fair clock over that empty office.

neighborhoods.name: Listening Courts
neighborhoods.premise: The court won silence from its advertisements and lost its flood warning with them. Sable is building a warning that can be seen and felt without turning every home into a loudspeaker.

events.name: Courtyard tending
events.detail: Caretakers share the day's water between the planters.

events.name: A quiet assembly
events.detail: Neighbors compare written notices around the court.

events.name: Warning inspection
events.detail: Technicians check the court's visual and tactile signals.

stages.line: We took the advertisements down. Nobody told us the flood warning shared their wire.

stages.contactLine: The advisory arrived. None of our neighbors received it. We need a warning people can see and feel, including when it fails.
stages.line: Sable kept the missed alarm in the minutes. Winning quiet didn't make us safe.

stages.contactLine: The lamp and rail agree. A successful test won't check tomorrow's battery. Put names on the inspection rota.
stages.line: Try the rail when the lamp pulses. My father can feel that through his gloves.

stages.contactLine: Two neighbors check the battery each shift. The lamps and rail belong to the court. Your room's speaker still belongs to you.
stages.status: Quiet, with a way to warn
stages.line: The rail and lamps take turns being checked. We kept the quiet, and made someone responsible for the warning.

neighborhoods.name: Last Connection
neighborhoods.premise: The night connection is listed as empty because its cleaners and carers travel on service passes. Ivo has one shift to make the people who keep the towers alive visible to the timetable.

events.name: Shift connection
events.detail: Commuters gather at the skyway's departure board.

events.name: Platform service
events.detail: The transit crew checks lights between departures.

events.name: The last handover
events.detail: Night workers exchange supplies before the long walk home.

stages.status: An empty service full of people
stages.line: Forty of us used that connection. The counter said zero. Service passes don't count as passengers.

stages.contactLine: Forty names on an empty service. Find where the counter loses them; I want that rule beside the closure notice.
stages.line: Ivo has our names. I didn't think I'd ever be relieved to appear on another list.

stages.contactLine: They accepted work as a fare, then excluded that fare from demand. Now we need a timetable someone is paid to keep.
stages.line: Cleaning the tower buys a service pass. Apparently it didn't buy the right to need a way home.

stages.contactLine: The late lift has a named crew and a relief time. Fewer trips than we asked for, but the last one is on the board. People can plan around it.
stages.line: The late lift stays staffed now. Fewer trips, shared duty. I can tell my daughter when I'll be home.
